name: Scientific Compute Layer (SCL)
description: A reusable native scientific-computation layer in C++17/CUDA behind a process boundary: scl_cli reads one JSON request from stdin, dispatches on the operation field through a fixed registry (lj_pairwise_energy_forces, fourier_transform_1d, least_squares, kalman_filter_linear), and writes one JSON result to stdout with a staged fault vocabulary that is never collapsed to a generic failure. A dependency-free Python client (scl) encodes requests, drives the binary and content-addresses requests and results; a separate, explicitly imported scl.ste_adapter translates STE's ExecutionSpecification/ExecutionResult so SCL can be plugged in as a runner at STE's SpecificationDispatcher seam. SCL also holds its half of the requirement/capability exchange with the acquisition layer (DAQ). It is one integration environment for STE, not defined by it; it never admits evidence, never touches STE's Rust workspace, and never claims that a computation is a measurement. The CUDA backend compiles and links but has never executed on a GPU in any session.

capabilities.label: scl_cli request: one JSON object on stdin
capabilities.description: Request {operation, backend: cpu|cuda, configuration_hex, input_hex}. The envelope, hex framing and backend-availability check are operation-agnostic; the operation owns decoding, validation and dispatch. One process per computation. A request naming an unknown operation or backend is answered as halted with exit_code 10 (PROTOCOL); an unavailable backend halts with 12 before any bytes are decoded.
capabilities.latency: ~4-7 ms process/JSON boundary plus native compute

capabilities.label: scl_cli result: one JSON object on stdout
capabilities.description: Response {status: completed|halted, exit_code, backend_used, backend_version ('scl-cli/0.1.0'), output_hex (null when halted), detail (null when completed), metrics{...}} such as native_compute_seconds and n_particles. Process exit code is 0 whenever a well-formed JSON answer was produced, including halted; a non-zero process exit means the CLI could not answer at all.

capabilities.label: Staged fault codes
capabilities.description: exit_code 0 completed; 10 PROTOCOL (malformed envelope, unknown operation); 11 VALIDATION (bad parameters/input); 12 BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE (cuda without toolkit or device); 13 COMPUTATION (coincident particles, non-finite result); 14 INTERNAL (unexpected exception). Single source of truth in protocol.hpp, mirrored in python/scl/errors.py and ste_adapter FAULT_* constants.

capabilities.label: Report the native binary version
capabilities.description: scl_cli --version prints the kernel version string (scl-cli/0.1.0), the same value echoed as backend_version in every response and folded into STE's program bytes by the adapter, so a kernel version bump is a new program identity.

capabilities.label: CUDA backend selection
capabilities.description: backend 'cuda' routes lj_pairwise and fourier (cuFFT) to native/backends/cuda when built with -DSCL_WITH_CUDA=ON and a device is visible; otherwise halts with 12. Implemented, compiled and linked against CUDA 12, 51/51 native tests, but never GPU-executed in any session (cudaGetDeviceCount()==0); CPU-CUDA equivalence, determinism and performance are explicitly not claimed.

capabilities.label: Compute truncated Lennard-Jones energy and forces
capabilities.description: operation 'lj_pairwise_energy_forces': configuration 24 bytes = epsilon, sigma, cutoff as f64 LE; input N*24 bytes of (x,y,z) f64 LE; output 8 + N*24 bytes = total_energy then per-particle (fx,fy,fz). V(r)=4eps[(s/r)^12-(s/r)^6] for r<=cutoff, plain truncation. Faults: sigma/epsilon/cutoff not finite or <=0 (11), zero particles (11), coincident particles (13). Bitwise reproducible on the same binary and machine.

capabilities.label: Compute the 1-D discrete Fourier transform
capabilities.description: operation 'fourier_transform_1d': configuration 24 bytes = int32 direction(+1 forward|-1 inverse), int32 normalization(0 none|1 1/N|2 1/sqrt N), int32 has_sample_spacing, int32 reserved=0, f64 sample_spacing_seconds; input N*16 bytes complex (re,im) f64; output N complex bins k=0..N-1, no fftshift. Any N>=1; CPU evaluates the O(N^2) defining sum. Spacing bytes under has_sample_spacing=0 are refused, never ignored.

capabilities.label: Solve a (weighted) linear least-squares fit
capabilities.description: operation 'least_squares': configuration = int32 weighted, three int32 zeros, f64 rank_tolerance (relative singular-value cutoff, explicit at every call site); input = int32 n_rows, int32 n_cols, X row-major f64, y f64, optional per-row weights f64; output = coefficient vector f64 LE. Weights are inputs, not parameters, so parameters_identity stays comparable across datasets. Row order is not significant.

capabilities.label: Run a linear Kalman filter over a measurement stream
capabilities.description: operation 'kalman_filter_linear': configuration = int32 n, m, Q provenance (always ASSERTED=0), R provenance (0 asserted|1 supplied), two reserved, f64 symmetry_tolerance, psd_tolerance, then F(n*n), H(m*n), Q(n*n), R(m*m) f64; input = int32 steps, int32 source_identity_length, x0, P0, measurements (ordered), source identity bytes. supplied on Q, or a source identity under asserted R, is a validation fault. Order of measurements is significant.

capabilities.label: Drive scl_cli from Python
capabilities.description: run_scl_request(SCLRequest, cli_path=default_cli_path(), timeout=60.0) -> SCLResult. Spawns one scl_cli process, marshals JSON, decodes output bytes. Raises SCLProtocolError (missing binary, unparseable stdout, non-zero process exit) or SCLTimeoutError for channel failures; a halted computation is returned as a normal SCLResult, convertible to a typed exception with raise_for_result.

capabilities.label: Content-addressed request and result identities
capabilities.description: SCLRequest exposes operation_identity, parameters_identity, input_identity and identity(); SCLResult exposes output_identity and computation_identity. Scheme: length-prefixed tag + fields, SHA-256, lowercase hex under scl.request.*.v1 / scl.result.*.v1 domain tags, a separate namespace from STE's scout.execution.* identities. Annotating parameters (e.g. sample spacing) change request identity but not computation identity.

capabilities.label: Encode/decode Lennard-Jones wire payloads
capabilities.description: encode_lj_configuration(epsilon, sigma, cutoff), encode_lj_positions(positions), decode_lj_configuration(bytes) and decode_lj_output(bytes) -> (total_energy, forces) produce and read exactly the byte layout scl_cli expects (little-endian float64).

capabilities.label: Encode/decode Fourier payloads and derive the frequency axis
capabilities.description: encode_fourier_configuration, decode_fourier_configuration, encode_complex_signal, encode_real_signal, decode_complex_spectrum, frequency_bins(n, sample_spacing) (returns None with no spacing; never assumes dt=1) and spectral_power_total; constants FORWARD/INVERSE and NORMALIZATION_NONE/ONE_OVER_N/ONE_OVER_SQRT_N.

capabilities.label: Encode/decode least-squares payloads and residuals
capabilities.description: encode_least_squares_configuration(rank_tolerance, weighted), encode_least_squares_input(design, response, weights), decode_least_squares_output, residuals and normal_equation_residual helpers for independent checking of a returned fit.

capabilities.label: Encode Kalman configuration and input
capabilities.description: encode_kalman_configuration(F, H, Q, R, measurement_noise_provenance=ASSERTED, symmetry_tolerance, psd_tolerance) and encode_kalman_input(x0, P0, measurements, source_identity=None). There is deliberately no process-noise provenance argument: Q is always asserted.

capabilities.label: Typed Quantity with explicit uncertainty kind
capabilities.description: Quantity(value, unit, uncertainty_kind in stated|estimated|propagated|absent, uncertainty) and absent_uncertainty(value, unit): a JSON-serializable shape for values placed inside STE's open Observation.content, not a second evidence system.

capabilities.label: Domain method blocks for computed results
capabilities.description: LJMethodBlock / lj_method_block_for and FourierMethodBlock / fourier_method_block_for record what was computed (potential form, cutoff handling, algorithm, normalization, frequency-axis applicability) with every non-applicable field marked applicable: false and a reason, never omitted or fabricated.

capabilities.label: Run an STE ExecutionSpecification on SCL
capabilities.description:
run_scl_specification(spec, cli_path, timeout) is a drop-in runner for STE's SpecificationDispatcher (alternative to execution.gromacs). It splits the program descriptor 'ste.scl.<operation>.v1
<version line>
[backend]
<cpu|cuda>', runs scl_cli, recomputes output_identity and computation_identity with execution.commitments from bytes it holds, and returns STE's ExecutionResult with the same FAULT_* codes. Only this module imports STE.

capabilities.label: Build an STE specification for an SCL operation
capabilities.description: build_lj_specification and build_fourier_specification assemble an ExecutionSpecification whose program folds the kernel descriptor, scl_cli version line and backend (two backends are two programs), whose configuration is the operation parameters and whose input_payload is the data. scl_version_line reads the version from the binary.

capabilities.label: Interpret an SCL ExecutionResult as evidence-classed content
capabilities.description: interpret_lj_result(candidate, result) and interpret_fourier_result produce the semantic content mapping (evidence_class 'computed', typed Quantity values, method block) that the caller wraps into a DispatchedMeasurement for STE's own admission path. SCL never calls admission itself.

capabilities.label: Participating, annotating and provenance parameter rules
capabilities.description: Every configuration field is participating (read by the mathematics; enters output and computation identity) or annotating (enters request identity only, e.g. sample spacing); noise matrices additionally carry a supplied|asserted provenance discriminant that participates. A guarded payload must have exactly one encoding per meaning and is refused when unused. Enforced registry-wide by tests/test_annotating_parameters.py and test_operation_registry_contract.py.

capabilities.label: Scoped reproducibility claims
capabilities.description: Claimed and tested: bitwise reproducibility on the same binary, machine and backend (-fno-fast-math, no SIMD flags); numerical agreement of forces with the finite-difference energy gradient; semantic identity (same request => same identity). Not claimed: physical correspondence to a measurement, cross-machine or cross-compiler bitwise equality, CPU-CUDA agreement.

capabilities.label: Build the native substrate
capabilities.description: cmake -S native -B native/build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release [-DSCL_WITH_CUDA=ON] && cmake --build native/build produces the scl_core static library and the scl_cli executable (requires nlohmann_json >= 3.9; CUDAToolkit when CUDA is on). ctest runs the native suites; python3 -m pytest tests/ builds native/ automatically if needed.

capabilities.label: Run the CPU performance baseline sweep
capabilities.description: python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py [--out results.json] sweeps particle count N and records wall_clock_seconds, native_compute_seconds, ste_overhead_seconds and payload sizes per run, to establish the measured cost of the process boundary rather than optimize it.

capabilities.label: Run the pre-registered Kalman validation scenarios
capabilities.description: kalman_validate <seed> <steps> runs the pre-registered scenarios and prints statistics only; it applies no thresholds. The thresholds live in architecture/kalman_validation_preregistration.yaml and are applied by tests/test_kalman_validation.py, so the judgement cannot be adjusted in the commit that makes it pass.

capabilities.label: Generate the SCL requirements artifact
capabilities.description: build_scl_requirements.py traces the substrate inventory from executable code and emits architecture/exchange/scl_requirements.yaml with a sha256 sidecar: measured facts and per-workload requirements addressed to the acquisition layer (daq), CUDA library presence, and core-vocabulary candidates. Deliberately contains no ranking or workload selection.

capabilities.label: Canonical YAML serializer shared with the acquisition layer
capabilities.description: canonical_yaml.py fixes the exchange encoding: YAML 1.2 block style, keys sorted at every level, shortest round-trip floats with explicit exponent sign, UTF-8/LF, sha256 over the serialized bytes referenced as sha256:<hex>; canonicalization_fixture.yaml is the shared agreement fixture held byte-identical in both repositories.

capabilities.label: Verify a coordinated reissue landed in both repositories
capabilities.description: python3 architecture/exchange/verify_pair_landed.py <repo-a> <repo-b> asks the remotes, not the locals: exit 0 only if both branches are in sync with their remotes and every shared file (serializer, fixture, proof_integrity.yaml) is byte-identical across the compute and acquisition repositories.

capabilities.label: Joint workload decision record
capabilities.description: architecture/decisions/2026-08-26-joint-workload-decision.yaml binds, by sha256, the measured SCL requirements and DAQ capabilities artifacts to the decision to build least_squares first (entry point of the least_squares -> linear algebra -> Kalman -> PCA chain), with authorship provenance disclosed and obligations recorded; it must be reissued, not edited, if either input changes.

capabilities.label: Held copies of the cross-repository register and STE/DAQ artifacts
capabilities.description: architecture/exchange holds the derived invariant_register.yaml, a byte-identical mirror of daq_requirement_response.yaml, and ste_invariants.yaml (a reconstruction, explicitly not STE's own statement), each with sha256 sidecars, so SCL's binding to core@1.0.0 in extends_only mode is auditable from this repository alone.

metadata.framework: CMake, nlohmann_json, CUDA 12 toolkit (optional), stdlib Python >=3.10 (zero dependencies)
metadata.exposure: subprocess CLI (scl_cli, JSON stdin/stdout) and python package scl
metadata.backends: cpu (validated), cuda (compiled and linked, never GPU-executed)
metadata.gpu_target: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Super Max-Q on the development machine; not visible in any session so far

relations.description: Computed results flow from SCL into STE: scl.ste_adapter.run_scl_specification returns STE's ExecutionResult at the SpecificationDispatcher runner seam, and interpret_*_result shapes evidence-classed 'computed' content that the caller hands to STE's own admission path. Confirmed by code and by the no-mock integration suite against a real STE checkout.

Only in the integrated configuration: scl.ste_adapter imports execution.commitments, execution.engine and execution.specification from an STE checkout (STE_REPO), and the exchange artifacts extend STE's core@1.0.0. The standalone path (import scl) has zero STE dependency, proven in a fresh interpreter by tests/test_standalone_boundary.py. Confirmed by code.

SCL publishes its measured requirements per workload (stable variable identity, missing-value semantics, measurement-noise provenance) to the acquisition layer through the requirement/capability exchange, and holds the shared serializer, fixture and proof_integrity.yaml byte-identical with that repository. Inferred from exchange artifacts and verify_pair_landed; there is no code call path between the two.

run: pip install pytest && python3 -m pytest tests/ -v

external_services.purpose: Optional CUDA backend build; presence is a build fact only, no device visible in any session so far.

reference.spatial: No geography: particle positions and lattice coordinates are dimensionless model coordinates, never places.
reference.temporal: Measurement streams for the Kalman operation are ordered sequences and Fourier sample spacing is an optional annotating parameter; SCL keeps no clocks, timestamps or history of its own.
open_questions: The CUDA backend has never executed on a GPU; tests/test_cpu_cuda_equivalence.py is the single harness left to run when an RTX 2080 Super Max-Q-visible environment exists.
The acquisition layer is called data-acquisition-channel-daq in SCL docs and notations-acquisition-channel in STE; confirm the catalog id data-acquisition-channel refers to that repository.

SCL owns no comparison layer: results with equal computation_identity but different annotating parameters (e.g. sample spacing) are not spectrally comparable, and nothing yet prevents a consumer from comparing them.
STE_REPO is a path, not a secret; it is listed under secrets_env only because it is the one environment variable the test suite reads.

corpus.holding: No corpus. It computes over requests handed to it and returns results that are explicitly not measurements.

COR-003.note: Requests and results are content-addressed, so every result can be walked back to the request that produced it.

COR-005.note: A staged fault vocabulary that is never collapsed into a generic failure.

COR-006.note: Dispatch is a fixed registry behind a process boundary; nothing enters a canonical state from here.

COR-008.note: Keeps no clocks, timestamps or history of its own; the record of what was computed lives with the caller.

COR-010.note: Never admits evidence, never touches STE's workspace, and never claims that a computation is a measurement.
